theme: Doubles are twins: two and two, three and three, four and four

activities.title: Find the twin
activities.intro: Twins are two piles with exactly the same number in them. One pile is up at the top. Count it out loud, then find its twin down below and tap it.
activities.offScreen: Go and hunt for twins around the house. Two shoes. Two socks. Two ears. Bring a grown-up one pair of twins you found and tell them what makes them twins.

rounds.prompt: Count the red circles at the top out loud. Now tap the card with exactly that many blue stars.
Count the green leaves at the top. Now tap the card with the same number of gold coins.
Count the brown blocks at the top, touching each one. Now tap the card with the same number of orange fish.
Count the purple flowers at the top. Now tap the card with the same number of blue birds.

activities.title: Twin towers, counted all together
activities.intro: Here are two towers, and they are twins. When two piles are twins, the answer has a special name. It is called a double. Count both towers together and say how many blocks there are altogether.
activities.offScreen: Build two towers that are twins, then knock them both over and count every block on the floor. Say the whole sentence out loud: three and three is six.

rounds.prompt: Two blocks in this tower and two blocks in that tower. Count them all. How many blocks altogether?
Three blocks in this tower and three blocks in that tower. Count them all. How many blocks altogether?
Four blocks in this tower and four blocks in that tower. Touch each one as you count. How many blocks altogether?
Five blocks in this tower and five blocks in that tower. That is the biggest pair of twins there is on this screen. How many blocks altogether?

activities.title: Say the double
activities.intro: No counting one at a time this time. Listen to the two twin numbers, say the answer in your head, then tap the card that shows it.
activities.offScreen: In the car, ask a grown-up to say doubles at you. Two and two. Three and three. Four and four. See if you can say the answer before they do.

rounds.prompt: Two fingers on this hand and two fingers on that hand. Tap the card that shows how many altogether.
Three fingers on this hand and three fingers on that hand. Tap the card that shows how many altogether.
Four teddies on the bed and four teddies on the floor. Tap the card that shows how many altogether.
Five fingers on this hand and five fingers on that hand. That is every finger you have. Tap the card that shows how many altogether.

parentCard.title: Twin towers
steps: Tip the blocks out and build one small tower together, three high. Then give them the job in one sentence: make its twin, exactly the same, so nobody could tell them apart.
Let them build the second tower on their own and do not straighten it. If it comes out four high, count both towers with them and let them be the one who finds the extra block.
Once the twins match, ask them to count every block in one go and let them touch each one as they count. Then say the whole sentence back to them: three and three is six.
Now go bigger. Four and four, then five and five. Stop before the towers get too tall to stand up, because the falling over is far more fun than the counting and it will win.
Last, hunt twins with no blocks in them. Two shoes, two ears, two wheels on a bike, two hands. Ask them how many altogether each time, and if they can answer without counting, let them.
notice: Do they build the twin by copying the whole tower at once, or do they match it one block at a time?
When they count both towers, do they go back to one, or do they carry on from the first tower's number?
Which doubles come out of their mouth with no counting at all, and which ones still want fingers?
